scope: Edition 005 weekly synthesis: five research/model entries, two hosted workflow/image features and one speech-runtime update. All selected news dates fall October 19–26; earlier FastH3 uploads are explicit. Phonon v0.4.1/v0.4.2 were published after Friday’s review. Other newly covered items precede that review or lack exact publication times; SplatFlux is explicitly carried from Friday. Author/vendor results are scoped, not independently reproduced or universally ranked. Excludes robotics and physical AI.

papers.review_depth: Primary submission history, full methods/evaluation and available official artifacts reviewed. No model execution or independent reproduction.
papers.title: LLaCO: a smooth noise path can hide a sudden loss of token identity.
papers.full_title: LLaCO: Continuous Diffusion for Large Language Models with Competition-Aware Semantic Scheduling
papers.change: New to this weekly coverage; submitted before the October 23 review cutoff, not an October 26 release. Competition-aware scheduling allocates time around changes in token rank rather than equal geometric increments.
papers.summary: LLaCO combines unit-sphere corruption, a directional adapter and semantic-retention scheduling to adapt an existing 8B diffusion-language backbone. It separates misleading nearest-token changes caused by shrinking norms from actual directional competition.
papers.evaluation: Authors compare nine benchmarks against selected 7–8B discrete and continuous diffusion models. MATH: 62.12 versus Dream 51.20; HumanEval: 48.17 versus Dream 54.27. The two selected continuous baselines trail across all nine. Default inference uses blocks of four tokens and four evaluations.
papers.caveat: Not universal language-model SOTA. Backbone pretraining is excluded from the reported 1.685B adaptation tokens; larger blocks degrade some tasks. No measured throughput win established. High-dimensional statistical assumptions are distinct from exact pairwise crossing algebra.
papers.access: Official GitHub repository has report/assets and Apache-2.0 repository license, but inference code, training code and LLaCO-8B weights remain unchecked TODOs. No runnable release or checkpoint license verified.
papers.creator_implication: Editorial inference: a useful way to explain text diffusion for scripts and structured writing, not evidence of better filmmaking or a tool ready for production.
papers.visual_angle: Interactive ready: seeded high-dimensional token geometry with full-dimensional cosine ranks, a source/noise-plane projection, pairwise crossing thresholds, equal-geometric versus toy semantic time allocation, and a separate norm-decay preset. Synthetic numerical teaching model; no learned embeddings, denoiser, generated text or LLaCO reproduction.

papers.title: FastH3 Omni: eight calls, thirty-two internal updates
papers.full_title: FastVideo FastH3 Omni reference-to-video/audio release announcement
papers.version: 8-Step-V1; October 20 announcement and finalized model card
papers.change: Newly discovered October 20 announcement and access documentation, not a new October 26 checkpoint. HF history records uploads on October 5 and October 8, then release-card finalization October 20 at 18:34:38 UTC. Earlier public visibility is unverified.
papers.summary: Reference-conditioned video/audio distillation combines 32 fine-grid predictions into eight fused transformer calls. PDD supervises the internal predictions; DMD supervises complete generated outputs. This makes the distinction between solver updates and expensive network evaluations concrete.
papers.evaluation: Author benchmark: 27 workloads, nine reference combinations across 5/10/15-second clips, 1344×768 at 24 FPS on eight GB200 GPUs. Three measured seeds after warmup; reported 5.6–11.9× lower end-to-end latency than Base's 50 evaluations, including reference encoding and MP4 production.
papers.caveat: Complete serving recipes differ, so this is not an isolated distillation ablation. Base uses lossless rather than exact precision policy. Qualitative matched examples do not establish quality parity; optional 36-layer VAE comparisons are excluded from timing. Do not transfer server results to one consumer GPU.
papers.access: Public weights, runtime guides and ComfyUI paths verified. Weights use the MiniMax-H3 Community License Agreement. RTX 5090/Spark recipes default to 480p; NVFP4 needs Blackwell and can differ from BF16. No weights downloaded or executed; the user's Turbo 8 generation preference remains unchanged.
papers.creator_implication: Editorial inference: promising for faster reference-guided shot iteration. Compare final-shot quality, reference adherence and total latency, not just step counts.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: colored fine-grid trajectories grouped into fused calls beside an encoding/sampling/decoding time chart. Vary update count, heads per call, model-call cost and fixed overhead. Show analytic approximation error separately from hypothetical latency; no claim to reproduce FastH3 or measured quality.
papers.review_depth: Official methodology, model card, public HF commit metadata and community announcement reviewed. No inference, reproduction or independent quality benchmark.
Primary submission history, full methods/evaluation and available official artifacts reviewed. No model execution or independent reproduction.
papers.title: Direct Forcing: teach continuity and distribution together.
papers.full_title: Direct Forcing: A Single-Stage Training Recipe for Few-Step Autoregressive Text-to-Video Generation
papers.change: New to this coverage; original submission precedes Friday’s review. Combines paired continuation alignment with rollout distribution matching in a single post-training stage.
papers.summary: Reference histories teach what should happen next; maximum mean discrepancy aligns generated and reference feature populations. Dynamic gradient balancing combines both signals.
papers.evaluation: From pretrained Wan2.1-1.3B, authors run 250 updates on eight B200s, using 6,505 reference pairs. VBench: 944 prompts × five samples, 480p. Total 84.63 versus Elastic Forcing 84.25, but semantic score 79.08 versus 80.99.
papers.caveat: The 250 updates exclude backbone pretraining. Four evaluations apply per causal chunk, not an entire movie. Reported 20.63 FPS/0.25-second first frame share the baseline architecture; not a demonstrated speed gain. No independent reproduction.
papers.access: Paper is available; no official runnable code, weights or associated licenses verified. Evaluation up to 50 seconds does not establish longer, larger or higher-resolution behavior.
papers.creator_implication: A training direction for responsive video generation; not yet a creator application.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: colored reference/generated feature clouds with paired continuation arrows, MMD kernel interactions and gradient-weight controls. Demonstrate continuity versus distribution coverage in a toy objective, not a trained video model.

papers.review_depth: Primary submission history, full methods/evaluation and available official artifacts reviewed. No model execution or independent reproduction.
papers.title: UniVOE: removing the object is only part of the edit.
papers.full_title: UniVOE: A Removal-Driven Framework for Interaction-Aware Universal Video Object Editing
papers.change: Newly covered, not newly released since Friday. Uses effect-aware removal to create object-present/absent training pairs, then reverses them to train injection.
papers.summary: Targets objects together with shadows, reflections and other interactions. A remover bootstrapped from inpainting generates additional paired supervision; injection also uses a proprietary reward model.
papers.evaluation: Author comparisons use 100 VOR and 56 ROSE pairs. Injection ROSE FVD: 85.12 versus Seedance 2.0 143.56. Selected open/commercial comparisons do not establish a current universal editing leader.
papers.caveat: Generated hidden background is plausible completion, not recovered ground truth. Proprietary reward training limits reproduction; crowded scenes and heavy camera motion remain limitations. No independent evaluation here.
papers.access: Public Hub files include 50-step removal/injection branches, a 12-step removal branch and LoRA, with Wan2.1-VACE-14B required separately. Uploads date October 21; model-card update October 23. Linked Tencent-Hunyuan code repo returns 404. Metadata says Apache-2.0 but the card’s license section is still a placeholder; do not promise unrestricted commercial use.
papers.creator_implication: Promising cleanup and product-insertion research; missing runnable code and incomplete licensing text limit immediate adoption.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: colored object, shadow, reflection and background layers linked by an effect dependency graph. Adjust light direction, object position and mask dilation; compare object-only and interaction-aware removal. Analytic compositing, not UniVOE output.

papers.title: SplatFlux: decode a video latent into a scene you can revisit
papers.full_title: SplatFlux: Feed-Forward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction and Generation from Video Latents
papers.change: October 20 v1, carried explicitly from the October 23 delta into this weekly synthesis. Submission history rechecked: no new revision. A shared video-latent decoder separates static and dynamic 4D Gaussian content; not a new October 26 release.
papers.summary: A shared decoder converts observed or generated video latents into 4D Gaussians, separating static structure from moving primitives. Motion interpolation supports changing time and viewpoint without rerunning a network at each timestamp.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluations include NVIDIA Dynamic Scene, DyCheck and DAVIS reconstruction, plus SceneBench, PenguinVideoBenchmark and VBench-I2V generation. On VBench-I2V, imaging score is 72.07 versus Aether 69.85, but subject consistency is lower: 95.95 versus 97.97.
papers.caveat: Offline reconstruction/generation only. Mixed backbone comparisons and video proxy metrics do not establish universal 4D superiority. Generation adapts Wan2.1-14B; it is not a model trained independently from scratch. The paper reports roughly ten days on 32 H20 GPUs for the full training pipeline.
papers.access: Primary paper and project demos verified. The project exposes a paper link; no official runnable code, weights or their licenses were verified. Do not label open weights or a product launch.
papers.creator_implication: Editorial inference: promising for re-framing moving content after generation; generation, reconstruction, and novel-view rendering must remain distinct in explanations.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: A colored Gaussian scene with fixed background splats and moving foreground splats; separate panels reveal static aggregation and dynamic interpolation. Controls: Independent time and camera-orbit sliders, Static/dynamic probability threshold, Velocity-arrow display, Interpolation amount and occlusion overlay. Synthetic analytic Gaussian demonstration, not SplatFlux inference or recovered geometry.
papers.review_depth: Primary submission history, methods, evaluation and caveats reviewed; project/repository availability checked; no model execution or reproduction.

papers.title: Ideogram Vector: editable output needs more than sharp edges.
papers.change: Higgsfield's changelog dates its Ideogram Vector integration October 23; newly added to our coverage, not an October 26 launch. The official Ideogram model/API pages confirm SVG generation and conversion. An October 22 underlying launch was reported by secondary indexes, but its dated primary announcement was not retrieved, so the verified host date is used.
papers.summary: Text-to-SVG accepts a prompt and optional image references. Image-to-SVG converts an input without a prompt; its simple/detailed/auto modes trade shape count against retained detail.
papers.evaluation: Official examples and API contract reviewed. No quantitative benchmark, independent controlled comparison, generated-output inspection or local model run. SVG editability and fidelity claims are vendor descriptions.
papers.caveat: Scalable geometry does not establish semantic grouping, editable text, exact typography or clean topology. The source does not promise those properties. Detailed images may be simplified. No open weights or training method verified.
papers.access: Official Ideogram API exposes separate generation/vectorization routes; Higgsfield lists both workflows. Hosted access only verified through public documentation; no account or billable request used.
papers.creator_implication: A candidate for logos, title treatments and reusable motion-graphics elements; inspect path organization and lettering before handing assets to an editor.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: zoom an original analytic graphic, toggle raster/polygon/Bezier representations, adjust curve tolerance and reveal path counts; contrast shape selection with semantic object or editable-text layers. This is a representation lesson, not Ideogram output.
papers.review_depth: Official model page, current API schemas and dated host changelog; underlying launch timestamp gap disclosed.

papers.title: Phonon: inspect what the narrator will actually say
papers.full_title: Phonon Python normalization API and runtime releases v0.4.1–v0.4.2
papers.change: New published releases after Friday's review. v0.4.1 adds ptts.normalize(text, lang=...) without loading a model; v0.4.2 supports a narrower Mimi decoder dimension, Mac Catalyst and cross-platform speech regression checks. These extend the already-covered October 20 release.
papers.summary: Creators can inspect the exact normalized script before speech generation. The runtime can also accommodate distilled decoders narrower than the latent representation; this does not itself announce a new model.
papers.evaluation: Release notes and GitHub publication timestamps verified. Maintainer CI now exercises each backend/platform and checks recovered words with Whisper. This is a regression test, not an independent listening study, prosody assessment or new SOTA result.
papers.caveat: Release notes explicitly say attached CoreML/QNN model bundles are unchanged from v0.4.0. Do not imply improved voices or newly trained weights. GitHub created_at precedes published_at for v0.4.1; October 24 is the release-publication date.
papers.access: Public runtime releases available. Existing 31M English weights are Apache 2.0 and ungated; 40M variants remain gated and CC BY-NC 4.0. Advertised counts exclude the audio tokenizer. No model downloaded or executed and no access terms accepted.
papers.creator_implication: Editorial inference: preflight dates, prices and abbreviations before rendering narration. Keep script normalization, acoustic generation and playback buffering separate in the workflow.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed: typed-script and normalized-script lanes feeding latent-frame, decoder and playback lanes. Controls: language, numeric string, abbreviation, chunk duration and buffer size. Label normalization examples schematic unless verified against the API; no synthetic timings presented as measurements.
papers.review_depth: Official release notes, exact public GitHub release metadata and existing model cards reviewed; no local execution or listening comparison.

papers.title: Runway App Studio: package a repeated creative task as an app.
papers.change: Runway dates App Studio October 23. Newly discovered this weekly review; exact publication time unknown, so no after-Friday-cutoff claim. This is a workflow launch, not a new generative-model benchmark.
papers.summary: Describe a reusable creative tool, preview its implementation, swap models by generation step and publish it for a chosen workspace audience. Published source can be downloaded.
papers.evaluation: Official changelog and detailed help guide only. No application built, no credits spent, no quality/reliability or productivity benchmark verified.
papers.caveat: Build sessions consume credits. Apps currently cannot be deleted or unpublished through App Studio; the help guide points to audience restriction instead. App count examples are not a verified universal plan limit. Do not confuse App Studio with video Edit Studio.
papers.access: Dated release says paid plans. Enterprise access can be controlled per workspace. Private preview and published audiences are separate. Runtime data/export completeness beyond source ZIP was not verified.
papers.creator_implication: Potential for repeatable storyboard, asset or client-review tools. Compare editability, rerun cost and portability rather than assuming a no-code demo is a production workflow.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed dependency graph: script, references, shots, voice and final edit. Change one input, highlight invalidated downstream assets and compare selective rerun counts with full rerendering. Analytic graph, not a Runway integration.
papers.review_depth: Dated primary changelog plus build, access, credit and lifecycle documentation; no product execution.
